predecessors.name: Gupta Empire
predecessors.text: the Brahmaputra valley and the Meghalaya edge that Cliopatria cuts from the Gupta shape in 353; the Kamarupa page calls Kamarupa 'a subordinate but sovereign ally of the Gupta Empire' and the…

successors.name: Kamata Kingdom
successors.text: 'Kamarupa was reorganized as a new state.

successors.name: Ahom kingdom
successors.text: upper Assam: 'the Ahoms began building their state between the Kachari and the Chutiya kingdoms' in 1228

successors.name: Chutia kingdom
successors.text: the east of Kamarupa (the Chutiya kingdom)

successors.name: Kachari kingdom
successors.text: central Assam, south bank (the Kachari kingdom); the north bank went to the Baro-Bhuyans

rulers.name: Timgyadeva
rulers.title: governor for the Pala king of Gauda

ledger.x: 350: Pushyavarman founds the Varman dynasty of Kamarupa near Guwahati.
353: Kamarupa takes the Brahmaputra valley edge of the Gupta shape.
353: the Kamarupa shape of Cliopatria stands in full.

c. 422: Kalyanavarman occupies Davaka. 'Kalyanavarman (422-446) occupied Davaka'; Davaka lay 'in the Kapili river valley in present-day Nagaon district' and is not mentioned as independent after the 5th century. The year is the start of his reign; Cliopatria's 353 shape already contains these cells.
518-542: Bhutivarman extends Kamarupa to the Sylhet Division.
566-590: Sthitavarman moves the capital.

c. 637: Bhaskaravarman takes Karnasuvarna after Shashanka's death. 'After the death of Shasanka the capital city Karnasuvarna passed in to the hands of Bhaskaravarman'; 'Gauda was soon divided amongst Harsha and Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa'. Shashanka's infobox gives 636 as his death; the page does not say 'soon' in…
655: Salastambha ends the Varman line and founds the Mlechchha dynasty.
655: the capital moves to Haruppeswara.
656: the hills and Bhutan leave the Kamarupa shape.
656: 33 cells (about 8,300 km2) of the Kamarupa shape's northern edge pass to the Tibetan Empire shape.
656: Sylhet and Karnasuvarna are not in Cliopatria's 656 shape.
656: north Bengal enters the Kamarupa shape.
751: the north Bengal land leaves Kamarupa.

c. 810: the king of Pragjyotisha submits to Devapala. 'His expeditions resulted in the invasion of Pragjyotisha (present-day Assam) where the king submitted without giving a fight'; 'Pragjyotisa or Assam accepted the suzerainty of Devapala'; 'the king of Assam was either Pralambha or Harjara'. The page dates…

c. 860: Kamarupa slips out of Pala suzerainty. 'Narayanapala lost control of Assam and Orissa'; 'Encouraged by the Pala decline, the King Harjara of Assam assumed imperial titles.' Narayanapala reigned 854-908 (Majumdar) or 860-917 (Sircar) and the page gives no year for the loss, so 860 is Sircar's accession and the…
900: Brahma Pala founds the Pala (Bhauma) line.
900: the Pala kings rule from Hadapeshvara (Harruppeshvar near Tezpur).
c. 920: Ratna Pala moves the capital to Durjaya. 'Under Ratna Pala (r. 920-960), it moved to Durjaya, near Guwahati.'
960: the traditional Kamarupa extent is drawn in the Arunachal hills.
960: Bhutan, north Bengal and Sikkim join the Kamarupa shape.
1035: Dharma Pala makes Kamarupanagara (North Guwahati) the capital.
1056: the west of the Kamarupa shape falls to the Pala shape.
1056: the rest of the dropped west is stateless in Cliopatria.
1056: the east grows into the Patkai hills.
1072: the south-west leaves the Kamarupa shape for the Sena shape.
1100: Ramapala ends the Pala line and takes western Kamarupa.
1126: Vaidyadeva takes western Kamarupa back.
1140: the Kamarupa kingdom ends.

wars.name: Yasodharman's attack on Kamarupa
wars.outcome: The page calls it 'the first major assault from the west' and says the effect is unclear; no land is named.

wars.name: Later Gupta and Gauda attacks on Kamarupa
wars.outcome: Susthitavarman 'came under the attack of Mahasenagupta of East Malwa' (Kamarupa page) and 'was defeated by Mahasengupta on the bank of Lauhitya' (Varman page, 590-595); the Gauda army 'carried out attacks against the Varman King Susthitavarman' between about…

wars.name: Bhaskaravarman and Harsha against Shashanka's Gauda
Kamarupa-Kannauj war of Harshavarman and Yasovarman
wars.outcome: Yasovarman of Kannauj 'competed with him for control of Northern India'; 'Harshavarman was defeated and killed'; the Gaudavadha of Vakapati celebrated the victory without naming the king.

wars.name: Pala invasion of Pragjyotisha under Devapala
wars.outcome: 'the invasion of Pragjyotisha (present-day Assam) where the king submitted without giving a fight'; 'Pragjyotisa or Assam accepted the suzerainty of Devapala'; 'it has been inferred that the king of Assam was either Pralambha or Harjara'.

wars.name: Ramapala's conquest of Kamarupa
wars.outcome: 'The Pala dynasty came to an end when Kamarupa was invaded by the Gaur king Ramapala'; 'Timgyadeva was made the governor of Kamarupa who ruled between 1110 and 1126'; Ramapala 'could not keep control for long'.

wars.name: Vaidyadeva's revolt in Kamarupa
wars.outcome: 'a rebellion broke out in Kamarupa' in Kumarapala's reign, 'crushed by Vaidyadeva, minister of Kumarapala'; 'after Kumarapala's death, Vaidyadeva practically created a separate kingdom'.

certainty.note: No page gives a surveyed or treaty boundary for Kamarupa.
